hello.note: Said as ní hǎo: when two third tones meet, the first rises. 您好 (nín hǎo) is the polite form

please.note: Goes before the request: 请给我… (qǐng gěi wǒ) means please give me…

thank-you.note: The second syllable is light and short. The reply is 不客气 (bú kèqi)

yes.note: Chinese often repeats the verb instead of saying yes. 对 (duì) means that's right

no.note: 不 (bù) means not, and turns to bú before a fourth tone. 没有 (méiyǒu) means don't have

excuse-me.note: Gets attention and says sorry. 对不起 (duìbuqǐ) is a stronger sorry

my-name.note: The audio uses Peter (彼得, Bǐdé) as the example name

repeat.note: 一 (yī) changes to yí before a fourth tone

speak-english.note: 吗 (ma) at the end turns a statement into a yes/no question. 您 (nín) is the polite you

one.note: Changes to yí before a fourth tone and yì before the others: yìbǎi

two.note: When counting things, say 两 (liǎng): two tickets is 两张票

four.note: Sounds close to 死 (sǐ), death, so some people avoid it

eight.note: Considered lucky, because it sounds like 发 (fā), to get rich

thousand.note: Prices are in yuan, said as 块 (kuài): 十块 (shí kuài) is ten yuan

how-much.note: Point and say 这个多少钱 (zhège duōshao qián), how much is this?

would-like.note: A softer I'd like. The audio uses 一杯咖啡 (a coffee) as the example

i-want.note: Direct, and normal in shops and restaurants. The audio uses 这个 (this one) as the example

do-you-have.note: Put the item in the gap. The audio uses 水 (water) as the example

discount.note: Haggling is normal in markets, not in shops or malls

card.note: Mobile payment (支付宝 Alipay, 微信支付 WeChat Pay) is everywhere in China, and foreign cards are accepted less often, so it is worth asking

checkout-time.note: 几点 (jǐ diǎn) means what time

wifi.note: 无线网 (wúxiàn wǎng) means wireless network

toilet.note: "在哪里 (zài nǎlǐ)" means "where is …?" for anything. 洗手间 (xǐshǒujiān) is a politer word

taxi.text: 您能帮我叫一辆出租车吗
taxi.say: nín néng bāng wǒ jiào yí liàng chūzūchē ma

train.note: A high-speed train is 高铁 (gāotiě)

bus.note: A long-distance coach is 长途汽车 (chángtú qìchē)

which-train.note: 趟 (tàng) counts train trips. Swap in any city; the audio uses 河内 (Hénèi, Hanoi) as the example

two-tickets.text: 我可以买两张去...的票吗
two-tickets.say: wǒ kěyǐ mǎi liǎng zhāng qù ... de piào ma
two-tickets.note: 张 (zhāng) counts tickets. The audio uses 河内 (Hanoi) as the example city
two-tickets.spoken: 我可以买两张去河内的票吗

trip-length.note: The audio uses 河内 (Hanoi) as the example city

delicious.note: 好吃 is for food; 好喝 (hǎohē) is for drinks

allergic.note: Add the food: 海鲜 (hǎixiān, seafood), 花生 (huāshēng, peanuts), 鸡蛋 (jīdàn, eggs). The audio uses 海鲜 as the example

love-dish.say: wǒ hěn xǐhuan zhè dào cài
love-dish.note: Literally "I really like this dish". 太好吃了 (tài hǎochī le) means so delicious

what-called.note: Point at the dish or item

table-for-two.note: Literally "two people". For more: 三位 (sān wèi), 四位 (sì wèi)

beer.say: qǐng gěi wǒ yì píng píjiǔ

water.note: Many people drink hot water. Ask for 冰水 (bīng shuǐ) if you want it cold, and 矿泉水 (kuàngquánshuǐ) for bottled

help.note: Shout it. The police are 警察 (jǐngchá)
